date.as_written: saṃvat 891 śrāvan śuddhi tṛyā(!) (‥ ‥ ‥) nakṣetra(!) taddine

notes: The colophon says only 'saṃvat 891', with no era named. NS is the right reading: the scribe is a Newar vajrācārya, and VS 891 (c. 834 CE) or ŚS 891 (c. 969 CE) would be far too early for a Devanagari paper manuscript. The catalogue also gives NS 891, i.e. 1771 CE. The nakṣatra name is lost in the lacuna before 'nakṣetra(!)'. 'vakjrācārya' is a corrupt spelling of vajrācārya, 'liṣitam' stands for likhitam, 'tṛyā' for tṛtīyā, and 'kalparatikā' in the first colophon is a slip for kalpalatikā. In Newar Devanagari ṣ often stands for kh, so the author's name may really be Jākharāja. 'kavikairavendu' is an epithet ('moon to the lotus of poets'), not part of the name.
